**Proof idea.** Let F(x) be the supremum on the left-hand side. Take h1(t) = c(t) and h2(t) = F(t) − c(t)·t, where c(t) is the right derivative of the convex function F at t, defined as a supremum of left difference quotients.

- **Convexity.** Each term g1(s)^x·g2(s) equals exp(x·log g1(s) + log g2(s)), which is convex in x. So F is convex, using `convexOn_exp` for each s and then taking the supremum.
- **Supporting lines.** The three-slope inequality gives F(t) + c(t)·(x − t) ≤ F(x) for all x and t.
- **Equality.** Each affine term x·c(t) + F(t) − c(t)·t is at most F(x) by the supporting-line bound. Taking t = x attains F(x), so the supremum over t equals F(x).
